title: Drop the industrial electricity scheme
headline: Drop industrial electricity help. Saves £0.1bn in 2029-30.
description: The Budget funds the British Industrial Competitiveness Scheme from April 2027, cutting electricity bills for energy-intensive firms, with a backdated payment for 2026-27. Switch this on to drop it. Most of the cost falls in 2027-28.

baselinePolicy.text: The British Industrial Competitiveness Scheme is funded from 1 April 2027, with a backdated payment for 2026-27 (Table 6.1 line 70).

source.quote: This measure provides funding for the residual costs of the British Industrial Competitiveness Scheme (BICS) and the Supercharger uplift on energy bills

alreadyIncludes: The British Industrial Competitiveness Scheme is funded from 1 April 2027, with a backdated payment for 2026-27 (Table 6.1 line 70).

lines.title: Industrial Electricity: Fund the British Industrial Competitiveness Scheme starting from 1 April 2027, including a backdated payment for eligible businesses

rawSource.note: Reversal on the spending side: the Treasury’s costing with the sign kept (a line that reduced borrowing is spending the reversal adds back; a line that cost money is spending the reversal saves).

caveats: The Treasury’s costing is on the OBR October 2026 forecast, the baseline used here. Effects before the start year are not applied: 2026-27 falls before any Budget of yours.

considerations.text: The Treasury’s scorecard figure is the certified direct costing for the measure, including the behavioural response the Treasury and OBR agreed; the Budget 2026 policy costings document gives the method.
